premises: TiB2 is susceptible to molten aluminum corrosion under hot-dip conditions (~700 °C).
Silicon, when oxidized, forms a stable, continuous, and adherent SiO2 layer on TiB2.
An SiO2 layer acts as an effective passivating barrier against molten aluminum penetration.
Pre-oxidation of silicon-modified TiB2 yields a protective SiO2 layer before aluminum exposure.
The SiO2 barrier reduces corrosion rate, leading to >30% improvement in mass loss over baseline TiB2.
